x: Chris Fairfield, who has improved to the extent of four minutes since joing us last year, took the handicap with Arthur Penstone second and George Piddington a very keen lad who had also improved considerably over the past few months, in third place.
With the aid of Ron Shipley, our second-claim member from Farnham A.C., and the ever present Don Newell, George Piddington and Chris Fairfield we were able to start 10 runners.
Those who rarely miss a fixture include George Piddington, Chris Fairfield Dennis Jones, Eric Penny and Mike Stearman, with another half-dozen not far behind.
Geoff.North's fast run also earnt him 3rd place in the handicap - Chris Fairfield having risen above his usual form to take first prize and Adrian Major a well earned second.

Young Blair-Fish, who joined us earlier this year, was a good winner of the race (off 3:30) with his actual time ranking 14th of the 40 runners. Chris Fairfield pulled one out of the bag for 2nd and our old friend Dudley Gordon just had to get amongst the prizes again, finishing 3rd.

Surprises in the middle of the field were Chris Fairfield, John Hilton and our veteran ex marathon champion Colin Collis. Battling together for much of the race these three didn't realise they were fighting for two of the handicap prizes!

Chris Fairfield now a second claim member and living at Stalybridge, Cheshire, promptly sent in his subs with an accompanying newsletter. He had run a 3 hrs 6 mins in the London Marathon but brought home the bacon when he won a £1,000 worth food voucher in a competition organised by a Bacon Company.
There must be quite a few members who remember Chris Fairfield, one of our runners back in the '60s. Chris joined us in 1958 but eventually moved to Stalybridge in Cheshire.
